flags.observation: Intro reads as neutral plot synopsis; deck title, kayfabe thesis and any satirical or provocative edge are absent from both intro beats.
Outro calls back to promoter and final bell, but the turn stays narrative; the work-versus-shoot concept never surfaces in the frame.
"Her sister's story buys time for:" links to the Vizier without causal logic; the story does not obviously produce the referee.
Opener plus card line totals about 120 characters; not sayable in one breath.
"The stolen commission buys:" implies a purchase of the lamp, an event the card never states.
"another bargain" presumes an earlier bargain that the song never established.
Openers share one template, previous card as subject plus verb and colon; "conceals" then "waits" chains as and-then, no but or twist.
Every callback opener points only at the immediately preceding card; no opener reaches back to the intro pair or a distant card.
"razor terrain" tacked on as a power label tag after the claim; reads like a rulebook index.
"hardcore valet, daggers" appends label plus image as a list; "daggers" echoes "dagger" in the same line.
"the botch, password" closes on bare power-label fragments; residue of card mechanics rather than story.
"the squash match destroys them" leaves "them" without a referent; closure blurs. Tone note respected: sung as "The Giant", no cannibal.
